rv.q: At the show I saw, frankly, the musical underline made a lot of the spoken dialog hard to understand as the sound balance throughout was less than ideal, including in the musical numbers where the very decent singers often struggled to be heard above the musicians.
Now in its North American premiere at Chicago Shakespeare Theater, THE LORD OF THE RINGS is sprawling, messy theater that’s in serious need of editing.

In the end, I have to conclude that no production of this adaptation is ever going to be fully satisfying, because the composers wrote a film score rather than one where the songs become the dramatic scenes.
Under the masterful direction of Paul Hart, THE LORD OF THE RINGS is transfixing!
This production is a truly ambitious artistic achievement, and my hat’s off to everyone involved.
If you are a LOTR fan, this is a must see show to put on your summer list before the production heads to New Zealand!
So it was natural for me to feel that in its present form, “The Lord of the Rings-A Musical Tale” still has some room to coalesce for its next date with destiny.
So long as you’re not a total Tolkienophile, obsessed with the Canon and unable to tolerate even minor infringements, you will enjoy THE LORD OF THE RINGS - a Musical Tale .

For all the satisfying highlights, however, this is an uneven, overlong show that will appeal most to diehard LOTR fans and nerdlings devoted to D&D campaigns and trips to the Bristol Renaissance Faire.
See this version for the spectacle, but my recommendation, if you really want to experience this incredible tale, is to read the books or watch the movies.
The Lord of the Rings” musical, now playing at Chicago Shakespeare Theater, is a disappointing muddle.
Though I clearly cannot recommend you spend your time and money to see The Lord of the Rings: A Musical Tale , I do feel I witnessed something wholly unique.
The extensive cast of over 20 actors delivers outstanding performances.

cn.t: Critics find this visually spectacular production impressive in scale and design, but most agree it's overstuffed and emotionally hollow, struggling to condense Tolkien's epic into coherent musical theater.
